newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - More buyers emerge for light grades.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - More buyers emerge for light grades.

text.p: Activity on the Asian crude market was dominated by light crude trades, with demand from a Hawaiian refiner and some Australian refiners helping pull up light crude prices, traders said on Friday.
End August/early September Kutubu was sold between Australian refiners at Tapis APPI -80 cents per barrel, firmer than earlier trades at discounts around $1.00.
August Gippsland was also traded at Tapis APPI -50, to an Australian refiner.
But despite the firmer prices of Australian crudes, Tapis was heard sold at APPI -35/-40 to a U.S. major.
This is only the second Tapis trade done below APPI in the last few years and the low level led some traders to question if light crude prices had hit bottom.
Most of the Australian crudes were committed for August, although an early August Kutubu cargo was finding very few firm bids and was offered at Tapis APPI -90.
Some Jabiru and Griffin were available, but may be taken into the sellers' own systems if unsold.
Japanese buying for Asian heavy crudes was lacklustre on Friday, keeping prices of Cinta and Widuri stagnant, traders said.
But the premiums of Minas were kept supported, mainly due to unexpectedly strong demand from an Australian refiner.
The refiner bought 100,000 barrels from a U.S. major at ICP +69 cents per barrel and another 200,000 barrels from a shosha at ICP +75 cents.
With the lower Minas export volumes, traders said that only 200,000 to 300,000 barrels of August Minas are available.
